Legacy contains semantic grounding, selector healing, browser discovery/watchdog, provider discovery and streaming alignment machinery intended to survive changing provider UIs.

atoms.claim: The destination registry defines VS0–VS8 around intent→world/context→capability→routing/authority→work→evidence→user result; these slices are the primary integration test of the reconstructed system.

A Provider identifies an external service class while Account identifies a user's relationship within that provider; Legacy has the concrete relationship but Ω destination still needs a first-class account model.

Legacy separates ProviderSession and ProfileSession; current provider-browser has an explicit live browser session mode. No evidence yet establishes one canonical Ω lifecycle for authentication, expiry, reconnect and account choice.
Current Ω separates routable capability contracts from ProviderRealization records; provider-browser verifies a PROMOTED realization and parser pin before message.send execution.
Canonical intent persistence, capability resolution and law/consent are separate seams; a root request is not equivalent to permission or execution.
Current run/work mechanisms and vault revisions can persist execution evidence, but the product needs a single work lifecycle linking request, progress, waiting, outcome and durable history.
Destination world/canvas reconciliation makes surface a projection of canonical world/evidence; current mind is a bounded derived lens rather than the authoritative world.
Product Instance characterization requires a durable boundary distinct from replaceable binaries and temporary runtime state; current Ω vault is strong but the product wrapper is not assembled.

Destination provider reconciliation separates available realizations from user routing policy; Legacy has preference/routing behavior, but current Ω evidence does not prove a complete durable policy object.

Current Ω has strong implemented and tested substrate layers, but destination documents separately classify product maturity, human usability and sovereignty; code existence must not be promoted into product completeness.
